task.description: Rework 2 of 3 for WF-03 Step 2 (design) of ISS-0418, per ORCH's explicit direction (delivered as a message during rework 1, not a validator gate). ORCH accepted rework 1's route (b) retraction and its unprompted surfacing of a third option (§6.4), and has now CHOSEN that third option: wire the InvocationLease primitive into the eight :wasm_hang hang dispatches directly, in this same run, alongside shipping the primitive. Task: (a) specify the test-side wiring concretely enough to build; (b) work through the determinism claim honestly rather than asserting it, and state precisely what it does and does not guarantee; (c) keep the production-uncapped limitation stated with undiminished prominence; (d) state what the wiring proves about the primitive beyond what unit tests alone would show.

result.summary:
lib/letflow/design/iss0418-wasm-concurrency-cap.md updated in place. I judged ORCH's option-three decision to be sound and built to it rather than pushing back a third time -- the objection route (a) raised in rework 1 (modifying invoke/2,3's own shipped algorithm, or forcing every caller through a new wrapper) genuinely does not apply to wiring a lease AROUND existing test calls, which is additive test-code using the exact crash-safety placement already worked out in section 2. Rework 1's own section 6.4 had already independently surfaced this as a legitimate option before ORCH chose it, so this is confirming a path already identified as sound, not being talked into a new one blind.

=== (a) THE CONCRETE WIRING ===

Re-read all three test files directly rather than trusting the prior validator's citation. Found the real count is 7 tagged tests but 8 hang DISPATCHES -- call_timeout_test.exs:76 (AC2) and plugin_handler_test.exs:472 (AC4) each dispatch 2 sequential live hangs in one test body. New section 6.1 tables all 8 dispatches by file:line, call shape, and dispatch count, reconciling ORCH's 'eight' against the validator's 'seven' (both correct for what they count).

Three distinct call shapes require three distinct wiring treatments, all specified concretely in new section 6.2, not left implicit:
  Shape A (4 dispatches: PluginInterface.invoke/2,3 called directly) -- test process IS invoke/2,3's caller already, exactly section 2's specified position. Wrap the existing invoke(...) call with try_acquire/0 before and release/1 (via ExUnit's on_exit/1 as the guaranteed-cleanup construct, since a later assertion failure must not skip release and leak into the next test) after.
  Shape B (1 dispatch: plugin_handler_test.exs:393, which reimplements invoke/2,3's own Task.Supervisor.async_nolink+Task.yield+Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) algorithm directly to observe the task pid) -- the test process plays exactly the role invoke/2,3 plays in production; lease acquired before Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2, released via the same on_exit/1 construct after the existing Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) call.
  Shape C (3 dispatches: call_timeout_test.exs:76's first call, host_api_write_test.exs:458, both raw Wasmex.call_function/4 with no PluginInterface/PluginHandler involved at all) -- lease acquired before Wasmex.start_link/1, released via on_exit/1; call_timeout_test.exs:76's SECOND call (on the now-permanently-wedged pid, proving section 1.2's Store-stays-wedged claim) deliberately does NOT acquire a second lease, since it is testing the same already-leaked resource, not a second independent admission.

=== (b) THE DETERMINISM CLAIM, WORKED THROUGH RATHER THAN ASSERTED ===

New section 6.3 answers the exact question ORCH posed (does a wedged slot help or just relocate the failure) with a split, precise answer rather than a single verdict:
  CONCURRENT ADMISSION: yes, genuinely deterministic by construction. All three files run async: false already, but that only means ExUnit's own test ORDERING is serial -- it says nothing about whether a prior test's native call has actually RETURNED before the next one dispatches (Shape B's Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) is confirmed-fast per section 1.4, but the underlying native Store execution is not killed by it). The wiring closes exactly this gap: try_acquire/0 cannot succeed until the PRIOR dispatch's release/1 has fired, which per the on_exit/1 placement only happens after that dispatch's own invoke/2,3 (or equivalent) has actually returned. This is exactly the race ISS-0418's own recurrence log documents (a neighboring test's not-yet-cleaned-up leak contending with the next dispatch), and it cannot occur once wired.
  WEDGED-SLOT ACCUMULATION: no, and stated with equal weight, per ORCH's own instruction not to let this go soft. Every one of the 8 dispatches permanently wedges one native TOKIO_RUNTIME slot forever regardless of the wiring -- the LEASE releases (because the outer boundary always returns, even though the native thread does not), but the pool itself has lost a real slot every time. New section 6.3.1 names the precise residual risk this creates: if the isolated subprocess's own available_parallelism() is smaller than 8, the later dispatches risk running against an already-shrunk pool even with perfect serialization -- serialization removes the race, not the arithmetic. Stated as a real, checkable, named constraint (not hidden), and distinguished explicitly from ISS-0418's own documented failure shape, which is entirely about CONCURRENT contention, not cumulative sequential exhaustion -- no existing recurrence note describes the latter shape.

=== (c) PRODUCTION-UNCAPPED LIMITATION KEPT VISIBLE, NOT ERODED ===

Updated in FOUR places, not just one, since a single fix would have been exactly the kind of partial correction this run has already caught elsewhere: section 0's headline bullet list (now states the CI-fix win and the production-uncapped limitation as two separate, equally prominent bullets); the REQUIRED MODULEDOC CONTENT in section 7 (added a new paragraph, ahead of the existing native-leak limitation paragraph, stating plainly that production dispatch does not call this module at all as of introduction -- so a reader of the shipped module's own docs cannot come away believing production is protected); section 6.6's honesty clause (now requires each test's own new wiring comment to say explicitly 'this lease is test-side only; production dispatch does not acquire one yet'); and OQ-C/OQ-D in section 9 (OQ-D marked RESOLVED by ORCH's decision, recorded for the historical record, with an explicit note that whoever builds OQ-C's production integration must still read section 8.1 in full -- the test wiring does not substitute for it).

=== (d) WHAT THE WIRING PROVES BEYOND UNIT TESTS ===

New section 6.4: invocation_lease_test.exs (unit tests) prove the MONITOR mechanism works against a synthetic Process.exit(pid, :kill) stand-in -- fast, deterministic, zero wasmex dependency. It cannot prove the PLACEMENT (which process acquires, which process is killed) is correct against the REAL invoke/2,3 algorithm and a REAL wasmex hang, only against this design's own description of one. Wiring into the real wasm_hang tests is what proves try_acquire/0 called from a genuine invoke/2,3 caller survives the genuine brutal-kill/exit path and release/1 genuinely fires every time, under the exact mechanism ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis live-reproduced -- the same 'verify against real source, don't assume' discipline REQ-170 applied to wasmex's own documented claims, applied here to this design's own claim about the kill boundary.

=== OTHER CONSISTENCY FIXES MADE WHILE REWORKING ===

Found and corrected three residual `cap: 1`-specific phrasings in section 6.3/6.3.1 that would have contradicted section 11's own (correct) note that no special test-environment cap override is used -- the wiring itself, not a particular numeric cap value, is what serializes admission here, since at most one lease is ever held at once regardless of configured cap. Generalized those three spots to be cap-value-agnostic. Rewrote section 11's file-touch inventory in full (not diffed) since its shape genuinely changed -- the three wasm_hang test files ARE modified in this rework, unlike rework 1.

No production code touched. No implementation code in the design doc -- section 6.2's wiring is shown as one illustrative try_acquire/release wrapper shape in prose/pseudocode form, consistent with this design doc's existing convention of showing call shapes without full function bodies.

next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for a fresh Step 2b gate pass. Re-derive, do not accept on my summary alone: (1) that all 8 hang dispatches across the 3 test files are actually covered by one of the 3 wiring shapes in section 6.2 with no gaps; (2) that the determinism claim in section 6.3 is precise rather than overclaimed -- specifically that it does NOT claim the wedged-slot/arithmetic risk in section 6.3.1 away; (3) that the production-uncapped limitation is stated with genuinely equal prominence in section 0, the section 7 moduledoc mandate, and section 6.6's per-test comment requirement, not only in one place a future edit could silently drop.
